author: "Working paper — full pipeline, demonstration data"

abstract: >
  Arizona's balancing authorities (APS, SRP, TEP) do not publish solar
  curtailment data, so any answer to "how much solar does Arizona waste, and
  what could flexible compute do with it?" must be estimated. This paper
  builds that estimation machinery: three independent estimators — a
  calibrated physical potential-vs-actual model with propagated uncertainty,
  a WEIM negative-price market signal, and documented anchors from filings —
  that are triangulated and never averaged, plus a flexible data-center
  scheduling simulation over the estimated surplus. IMPORTANT: every number
  in this version comes from a synthetic validation fixture with known
  injected curtailment (this build environment has no route to the EIA, NREL,
  or CAISO APIs). The fixture is used honestly: as a recovery test, in which
  the estimators must find curtailment we injected on purpose. They do — the
  potential-gap estimator's 5–95% band covered the injected truth in 8 of 9
  balancing-authority-years, which is what a 90% band should do. No number
  below is an estimate of actual Arizona curtailment.

## 1. The problem

Utility-scale solar is occasionally told to stop producing: *curtailed*.
CAISO publishes how much; Arizona's three large balancing authorities —
Arizona Public Service (AZPS), Salt River Project (SRP), and Tucson Electric
Power (TEPC) — do not. They report hourly demand, generation by fuel, and
interchange to EIA-930, but not curtailed MWh. Anyone claiming a number for
"wasted Arizona solar" is estimating, whether they admit it or not. We admit
it: the estimation strategy is the contribution.

The second half of the question is whether *flexible* compute — batch AI
training that can defer work into surplus hours — could productively absorb
that energy, and at what utilization cost. We simulate a configurable data
center scheduled into the estimated surplus windows and report the tradeoff
curve, under skeptical assumptions about how flexible frontier training
actually is.

## 2. Data

| Source | Role | Status in this build |
|---|---|---|
| EIA-930 hourly (AZPS, SRP, TEPC) | reported solar generation | fetcher written, **unverified-live**; synthetic stand-in |
| EIA-860 | fleet: location, capacity, tracking | fetcher written, **unverified-live**; synthetic stand-in |
| EIA-923 monthly per plant | calibration of the potential model | fetcher written, **unverified-live**; synthetic stand-in |
| NREL NSRDB | irradiance/temperature at plants | not yet wired; synthetic stand-in |
| CAISO OASIS WEIM prices | Estimator B signal | fetcher written, **unverified-live** (report/node names must be verified); synthetic stand-in |
| IRPs / ACC / FERC filings | Estimator C anchors | schema fixed; zero real anchors curated yet |

EIA-930 imputed hours are never silently ingested: rows carry an
`is_imputed` flag, flagged hours are excluded from all sums, and annual
totals are rescaled by usable-hour coverage. The EIA v2 API does not expose
imputation flags (only the bulk balance CSVs do) — a known gap recorded in
`SOURCES.md` that must be closed during live verification.

## 3. Methods: three estimators, triangulated, never averaged

### 3.1 Potential model and calibration

Each plant gets a tracking-aware pvlib model (transposition, cell
temperature, PVWatts DC, inverter clipping at AC nameplate) driven by the
weather the estimator can see. Unknown per-plant parameters are fixed
assumptions absorbed by one multiplicative calibration factor per plant,
fit on presumed-unconstrained months (Jun–Sep, Dec–Jan). 30% of eligible
plant-months are held out; per-plant holdout MAE is the reported model
quality. If those "unconstrained" months in fact contain curtailment,
Estimator A is biased **low** — the conservative direction for our claim.

### 3.2 Estimator A — potential-vs-actual gap

Curtailment proxy: calibrated potential minus reported actual, per BA-hour.
Weather error, unobserved outages, and derates are carried by the empirical
residual distribution measured on unconstrained hours; its 5th/50th/95th
percentiles generate the reported band. Clipping hourly gaps at zero turns
symmetric noise into fake positive curtailment — our validation fixture
exposed this bias directly, so A subtracts a clipped-gap false-positive
baseline measured on unconstrained hours (reported in
`estimator_a_annual`, not hidden). A sees the **union** of economic and
physical curtailment plus any residual suppression it cannot attribute; it
cannot split the two on its own.

### 3.3 Estimator B — WEIM negative-price signal

Hours with locational prices at or below zero mark market-cleared surplus:
an *economic*-curtailment signal, in hours. Converting hours to energy uses
coincident modeled potential, which yields only an **upper bound**.
Physical curtailment often produces no price signal at all, so B ≠ A by
construction, and their gap is information, not error.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
if MODE == "demo":
    cov = q("""
        WITH truth AS (
            SELECT ba_code, EXTRACT(year FROM ts_utc - INTERVAL 7 HOUR) AS year,
                   100*SUM(true_curtailment_mwh)/SUM(true_available_mwh) AS true_pct
            FROM demo_truth_ba_hour GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING SUM(true_available_mwh) > 1000)
        SELECT (t.true_pct BETWEEN a.curt_lo_pct AND a.curt_hi_pct) AS inside,
               ABS(a.curt_mid_pct - t.true_pct) AS mid_err
        FROM estimator_a_annual a JOIN truth t USING (ba_code, year)
    """)
    print(
        f"**Recovery test.** Estimator A's 5–95% band contained the injected "
        f"truth in {int(cov.inside.sum())} of {len(cov)} BA-years "
        f"(a 90% band should miss occasionally; the one miss is a year whose "
        f"heavy unobserved outages read as curtailment — exactly the "
        f"confounder the band models). Median absolute error of the midpoint: "
        f"{cov.mid_err.median():.2f} percentage points "
        "(table_id: estimator_a_annual vs demo_truth_ba_hour)."
    )
```

If A, B, and C disagree wildly on real data, that finding — "Arizona has no
idea how much solar it wastes" — ships as the result. We present the range;
we do not average.

## 4. Flexible compute simulation

A data center with IT capacity, PUE, and a flexibility class (fully
deferrable / partially deferrable / firm — floors of 0%, 50%, 100% of full
load) must deliver a weekly energy SLA. A greedy scheduler serves the floor
always and places the flexible remainder into the largest surplus hours;
every contiguous flexible run pays a checkpoint/restart energy overhead; an
optional battery charges only from unabsorbed surplus. We treat *fully
deferrable* as an optimistic envelope, not a claim about frontier training —
checkpointing cost, interconnect utilization economics, and job structure
argue for the partially-deferrable rows as the realistic anchor.

## 5. Ways this could be wrong (pre-registered)

Written before any real-data results exist, to be kept verbatim:

1. **Calibration-period contamination.** If "unconstrained" months contain
   curtailment, A under-estimates. (Direction: low.)
2. **Outages and derates masquerade as curtailment.** The band carries the
   average outage rate, not outage *years*; our fixture produced exactly one
   such band miss in nine. (Direction: high, occasionally badly.)
3. **EIA-930 data quality.** Imputed-hour flags are unavailable via the v2
   API; if the bulk-CSV flags disagree materially, hourly results shift.
4. **OASIS/WEIM assumptions unverified.** Report names, node choice, and
   price basis for the Arizona LAPs must be confirmed on the live system;
   Estimator B could change qualitatively.
5. **Economic vs. physical.** A sees the union; B sees mostly economic. We
   report both and never allocate the difference without evidence.
6. **The compute model is stylized.** Weekly-energy SLA and a constant
   checkpoint overhead are crude proxies for real training economics;
   the fully-deferrable rows especially should be read as an envelope.
7. **Synthetic-fixture circularity risk.** The fixture's weather and fleet
   are generated by the same physical model family the estimator uses,
   with injected biases/noise. Real weather error is likely worse. Recovery
   results are therefore an upper bound on real-world performance.

## 6. Replication

`make setup && make demo && make paper` reproduces this document end to end
with no keys (synthetic mode). For real data: put free EIA and NREL keys in
`.env`, verify each fetcher against a live response (checklist in
`SOURCES.md`), then `make real && make paper`. Every figure regenerates from
the DuckDB store at render time; every quantitative sentence above traces to
a `figure_id` or `table_id`.
